messages:
ellen (platform): quick question for the group: should internal RPCs be gRPC/proto-first or plain JSON/REST? need to consider routing policy ease, quota enforcement, and the console experience.
alex (infra): leaning gRPC for service-to-service. less wire, good streaming. downside: browsers. we can front with a transcoder but that's an extra layer.
rachel (console): browsers = JSON. If gateway handles transcoding, console devs don't care. main ask: we must not lose tenant/route headers when transcoding. charts depend on them.
tom (sre): ops concerns: long-lived grpc streams affect connection pooling. also we need a single place to enforce coarse quotas. gateway enforcement + service-level verification sounds right.
priya (api): proto-first helps with codegen and evolution. but we need a clear quota contract: header names, client-version, and route-id. propose headers: x-rw-tenant, x-rw-route, x-rw-quota-key.
zack (sdk): SDKs want idiomatic surface for each environment. we'll generate gRPC clients for backend teams and small Fetch JS wrapper for console. auto-generate example curl/js snippets.
alex (infra): important: define canonical error mapping (gRPC codes -> HTTP status + body). also include test vectors for transcoder correctness.
elllen (platform): small typo above but agreed. can we do canary by transport? e.g., 5% gRPC direct, 95% via gateway. need telemetry to compare cost and latency across transports.
tom (sre): yes, telemetry must include a dimension transport:grpc|http and preserve trace id across gateway. add alert: if transcoder adds >3ms median, fail canary.
rachel (console): console UX: add transport filter on route page, show delta latency/cost for canary vs baseline, and let SEs sample request traces.
priya (api): proto example for binding route metadata:
```
service Router { rpc Route(Request) returns (Response); }
message Request { string payload = 1; string route_id = 2; }
```
gateway should map route_id -> x-rw-route header for quota engine.
zack (sdk): quick fallback curl snippet for docs:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/predict \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-rw-tenant: acme" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
alex (infra): also note: transcoding can drop unknown headers unless we whitelist them. add test that verifies header passthrough.
tom (sre): enforcement points: gateway does coarse quota and rate-limit, service validates tokens and enforces fine-grained charge. dedupe checks so we don't double-bill.
priya (api): I'll draft an RFC with checklist: header whitelist, error mapping table, telemetry tags, canary plan, and test harness.
lighthouse-bot: RFC lint: missing x-rw-quota-key example in proto. please add.
priya (api): good catch, will add x-rw-quota-key to examples.
elllen (platform): decision sketch for RFC: default internal = gRPC/protobuf; provide managed transcoding gateway for external/browser clients; require header passthrough, transport tagging in metrics, canonical error mapping, canary-by-transport tooling.
rachel (console): +1 if console gets transport filters and sampled traces in route view.
zack (sdk): will add dual-surface examples and generators.
alex (infra): I'll start a small harness to replay traffic over both paths and produce per-transport histograms.
tom (sre): add an alert rule: if per-route transcoder overhead >3ms P50 or 10ms P95 during canary, trigger rollback.
elllen (platform): thanks all. Priya please post RFC link here when ready. aim EOD tomorrow. :rocket:
